name: Technologies: Tailwind CSS
description: Utility-first styling as used in GGLearn and GGSocial.

cards.subject: Utility-first CSS
says: styles an element by composing small single-purpose classes in the markup
avoids inventing a name for every piece of UI
cards.use: want to style a button without opening a separate stylesheet
not: requires a hand-written class for every element

cards.subject: A utility class
says: does one narrow styling job such as setting padding or a colour
is combined with many others on the same element
cards.use: want to add padding to one element and nothing else

cards.subject: Tailwind CSS
says: is a utility-first CSS framework
generates CSS only for the class names it finds in your source
uses colon prefixes for states and breakpoints
not: ships every possible utility in one fixed stylesheet

cards.subject: A variant prefix
says: applies a utility only under a condition such as hover or a breakpoint
is written before the class and joined to it with a colon
cards.use: want a colour to change only when the pointer is over the element
not: is a separate attribute placed beside class

cards.subject: Preflight
says: resets browser default styles on top of a modern base
strips default heading sizes and list markers
cards.use: wonder why an h1 renders at body size with no margin
not: adds a decorative theme to every element

cards.subject: Co-located styling
says: keeps the style next to the markup it affects
lets you delete an element and its styling together
removes the risk that editing a shared class breaks an unrelated page
cards.use: worry that changing a stylesheet rule will break another page

cards.subject: A constrained design scale
says: limits spacing, size and colour choices to a shared set of steps
keeps spacing consistent across a team
cards.use: want designers and developers to share one spacing vocabulary
not: accepts any pixel value you type into a class without limits

cards.subject: Long class strings
says: are the main readability cost of utility-first markup
are tamed by extracting a component for repeated patterns

cards.subject: Utilities compared with inline styles
says: can express hover, breakpoints and dark mode where a style attribute cannot
draw their values from a shared scale
cards.use: need a hover effect that a style attribute cannot express
not: are just inline styles with shorter names

cards.subject: Utility specificity
says: is kept low and flat so utilities rarely fight each other
lets the order in the generated stylesheet, not the class order in markup, decide a conflict
not: is raised by writing the later class last in the attribute

cards.subject: The order of classes in an attribute
says: does not decide which of two conflicting utilities wins
has no effect on the generated CSS
cards.use: put p-4 and p-8 on one element and wonder which applies
not: makes the last class win

cards.subject: Mobile-first breakpoints
says: apply an unprefixed utility at every screen size
apply a prefixed utility from that breakpoint upward
cards.use: build a layout that is one column on phones and wider on desktops
not: apply a prefixed utility only below that breakpoint

cards.subject: The md: prefix
says: applies its utility from the medium breakpoint and wider
starts at 768px by default
cards.use: want a change to start on tablet-width screens and stay for larger ones
not: applies only between medium and large widths

cards.subject: The sm: prefix
says: is the first default breakpoint above the unprefixed base
starts at 640px by default
cards.use: want a utility to switch on just above phone width
not: targets only small phones

cards.subject: The 2xl: prefix
says: is the largest default breakpoint prefix
starts at 1536px by default
cards.use: want a utility to change only on very wide monitors

cards.subject: The max-md: variant
says: applies a utility only below the md breakpoint
targets small screens directly without a mobile-first override
cards.use: need a style on phones only and nowhere else

cards.subject: A breakpoint range variant such as md:max-lg:
says: limits a utility to the band between two breakpoints
combines a minimum and a maximum width condition
cards.use: need a style that applies on tablets only

cards.subject: hidden md:block
says: hides an element on small screens and shows it from md upward
pairs a base display none with a breakpoint display
cards.use: want a sidebar visible only on wide screens

cards.subject: The container class
says: sets a max-width that changes at each breakpoint
does not centre itself unless you add mx-auto
cards.use: want content capped to a width that follows the breakpoints
not: centres its content horizontally on its own

cards.subject: Container query variants
says: size styles by the parent container rather than the viewport
suit a component reused in both narrow and wide slots
cards.use: need a card to reflow when its sidebar slot is narrow even on a wide screen
not: react to the viewport width just like breakpoint prefixes

cards.subject: The hover: variant
says: applies a utility while the pointer is over the element
is the usual way to add a pointer-over colour change
cards.use: want a link to turn white when the pointer is over it

cards.subject: The focus: variant
says: applies a utility while the element has keyboard or programmatic focus
styles a focused input with a ring or border
cards.use: want a text input to show a coloured ring while it is focused

cards.subject: The active: variant
says: applies a utility while the element is being pressed
gives a button instant press feedback
cards.use: want a button to darken while the mouse button is held down

cards.subject: The focus-visible: variant
says: applies focus styles for keyboard focus but not for most mouse clicks
is the usual choice for focus rings on buttons and links
cards.use: want a ring for keyboard users that does not flash on every mouse click
not: is identical to focus: in every browser interaction

cards.subject: The disabled: variant
says: applies to controls that carry the disabled attribute
dims or greys a button that cannot be used
cards.use: want a submit button to look inactive while the form is invalid

cards.subject: The group-hover: variant
says: styles a child when a marked ancestor is hovered
needs the group class on the ancestor
cards.use: want a card title to underline when anywhere on the card is hovered
not: styles the ancestor when its child is hovered

cards.subject: The peer-checked: variant
says: styles an element from the checked state of an earlier sibling marked peer
requires the peer to come before the styled element in the DOM
cards.use: want a label to change style when a checkbox beside it is ticked
not: styles a parent from its child's state

cards.subject: The odd: variant
says: styles every other child starting from the first
is the usual way to stripe table rows
cards.use: want alternate table rows to have a tinted background

cards.subject: The aria-expanded: variant
says: styles an element from its ARIA attribute value
keeps the visual state tied to the accessibility state
cards.use: want a chevron to rotate when the button's aria-expanded is true
not: only works if you also toggle a custom class in JavaScript

cards.subject: A data attribute variant such as data-[state=open]:
says: styles an element from the value of a data attribute
suits component libraries that expose open or closed state as a data attribute
cards.use: use a headless menu component that sets data-state on its panel

cards.subject: Stacked variants
says: combine several conditions by chaining prefixes in one class
apply the utility only when every chained condition is true
cards.use: want a hover colour that applies only at wide screen sizes

cards.subject: p-4
says: adds padding on all four sides
equals 1rem of padding with the default spacing scale
cards.use: want equal inner space around a card's content

cards.subject: mx-auto
says: centres a block with a set width using automatic side margins
has no centring effect on a block that fills its parent
cards.use: need a fixed-width column centred on the page
not: centres text inside the element

cards.subject: w-full
says: sets the width to 100 percent of the parent
makes a block-level child match its container width
cards.use: want an image or input to fill the width of its column

cards.subject: max-w-md
says: caps the width without forcing the element to that width
lets a narrower container shrink the element below the cap
cards.use: want a form to stay readable on wide screens but shrink on phones
not: forces the width to a fixed size

cards.subject: min-h-screen
says: sets the minimum height to the full viewport height
lets the element grow taller if the content needs it
cards.use: want a page background to fill the screen even when content is short
not: fixes the element at exactly the viewport height

cards.subject: ring-2
says: draws a ring around the element without changing its layout size
is a common focus indicator
cards.use: want a focus outline that does not push neighbouring content
not: adds two pixels to the element's width and height

cards.subject: The spacing scale
says: maps numeric steps to multiples of a base unit
makes one step equal 0.25rem by default
cards.use: wonder how large p-6 is

cards.subject: text-sm
says: sets a smaller font size together with a matching line height
is a step on the type scale
cards.use: want secondary captions smaller than body text

cards.subject: font-semibold
says: sets the font weight to 600
gives headings and labels a medium-heavy weight
cards.use: want a card heading bolder than body text but not fully bold

cards.subject: leading-relaxed
says: sets a taller line height for easier reading
changes spacing between lines rather than between letters
cards.use: want paragraphs to have more air between lines

cards.subject: tracking-tight
says: tightens the spacing between letters
is common on large headings
cards.use: want a large heading's letters set closer together

cards.subject: truncate
says: clips overflowing single-line text with an ellipsis
needs a bounded width to take effect
cards.use: need a long title to stay on one line inside a narrow card

cards.subject: line-clamp-3
says: limits text to three lines and ends it with an ellipsis
works for multi-line previews
cards.use: want a three-line preview of a long description
not: limits text to three words

cards.subject: The colour shade scale
says: pairs a colour name with a numeric shade
runs from light at low numbers to dark at high numbers
cards.use: see a class such as slate-300 and want to know what the number means

cards.subject: The opacity modifier
says: adds transparency to a colour with a slash suffix
removes the need for a separate opacity utility per colour
cards.use: want a black overlay at half strength
not: only works on backgrounds

cards.subject: text-slate-300
says: sets the text colour to a light shade of the slate palette
colours text, not the background
cards.use: want light grey-blue text on a dark header

cards.subject: bg-slate-900
says: sets the background colour to a very dark shade of the slate palette
colours the element's background, not its text
cards.use: want a near-black panel

cards.subject: border-white/10
says: sets the border colour to white at ten percent opacity
gives a faint divider on dark backgrounds
cards.use: want a barely visible edge on a dark card

cards.subject: bg-clip-text text-transparent
says: lets a background gradient show through the letters
needs a gradient background to be visible
cards.use: want a headline filled with a colour gradient

cards.subject: flex
says: turns an element into a flex container
lays its children out in a row by default
cards.use: need children placed side by side

cards.subject: flex-col
says: stacks flex children vertically
switches the main axis to vertical
cards.use: want a column of items inside a flex container

cards.subject: items-center
says: aligns flex or grid items on the cross axis to the centre
centres a row of items vertically
cards.use: want an icon and label vertically centred in a row

cards.subject: justify-between
says: pushes the first and last items to the edges with equal gaps between
distributes free space along the main axis
cards.use: want a logo on the left and a menu on the right

cards.subject: gap-4
says: adds equal space between flex or grid children
does not add space before the first or after the last child

cards.subject: space-x-4
says: adds horizontal margin between siblings through a selector
breaks down when children wrap onto a second line

cards.subject: flex-wrap
says: lets flex children move to the next line when they run out of room
stops a single-row flex container from squeezing items
cards.use: want a tag list to flow onto several lines

cards.subject: flex-1
says: lets a flex child grow and shrink to fill the available space
makes siblings share space equally when all have it
cards.use: want a main area to fill whatever width the sidebar leaves

cards.subject: shrink-0
says: stops a flex child from shrinking below its natural size
keeps an avatar from being squashed by long text beside it
cards.use: need an avatar to keep its size next to a long name

cards.subject: grid
says: turns an element into a grid container
places children into rows and columns
cards.use: need a two-dimensional layout of cards

cards.subject: grid-cols-3
says: creates three equal-width columns
pairs with gap utilities to space the cells
cards.use: want three equal cards per row

cards.subject: col-span-2
says: makes a grid item cover two columns
needs a grid parent to have any effect
cards.use: want one featured card to be twice as wide as the others

cards.subject: sticky top-0
says: pins an element to the top of its scroll container while scrolling
keeps a header visible as the page moves
cards.use: want a header to stay visible while the page scrolls

cards.subject: A design token
says: is a named design value such as a colour or spacing step
gives one place to change a value used across the app
cards.use: want to restyle a brand colour in one edit
not: is a JavaScript function that runs at render time

cards.subject: The Tailwind theme
says: defines the scales that utilities draw from
is extended or overridden to match a brand
cards.use: need the colour palette to match the brand

cards.subject: Extending the theme
says: adds new values alongside the defaults
keeps every built-in scale value available
cards.use: want one extra brand colour and all the default ones too
not: removes the default scale for that property

cards.subject: CSS variables as theme values
says: can change at runtime without rebuilding the CSS
let one utility class show different colours in different themes
cards.use: need the same class to look different in light and dark themes

cards.subject: Semantic colour tokens
says: name a colour by its role such as surface or danger rather than its hue
let a theme swap hues without touching components
cards.use: want components to survive a rebrand without edits
not: name a colour by its hue so it can never change role

cards.subject: An arbitrary value
says: sets a one-off value in square brackets inside a class
needs no entry in the theme
cards.use: need a single pixel width the scale does not offer
not: is rejected by the build unless it is in the theme

cards.subject: An arbitrary property such as [mask-type:luminance]
says: writes any CSS property and value in brackets as a class
covers CSS with no dedicated utility
cards.use: need a CSS property that Tailwind has no utility for

cards.subject: Promoting an arbitrary value to a token
says: replaces copies of a one-off value with a single named step
gives a repeated value one place to change
cards.use: see w-[37px] copied into many components

cards.subject: An underscore inside brackets
says: stands for a space in an arbitrary value
lets a multi-part value such as grid-cols-[1fr_2fr] fit in one class
cards.use: write a grid template with two tracks in an arbitrary value
not: marks the value as a CSS variable

cards.subject: A Tailwind plugin
says: adds utilities, variants or base styles beyond the core set
packages reusable styling for sharing across projects
cards.use: need a reusable set of styles beyond the built-in utilities

cards.subject: The typography plugin
says: styles raw rendered HTML such as markdown through a prose class
gives headings, lists and quotes sensible defaults inside one wrapper
cards.use: render CMS or markdown content that you cannot add classes to
not: is needed to use any text-* utility

cards.subject: The forms plugin
says: gives form controls a consistent base appearance that utilities can then restyle
resets native input styling for easier theming
cards.use: want checkboxes and selects to look the same across browsers

cards.subject: A custom utility
says: adds your own single-purpose class that still works with variants such as hover:
is the way to name a low-level style that Tailwind lacks
cards.use: need a single-purpose class that Tailwind does not provide

cards.subject: A custom variant
says: defines a new condition that can prefix any utility
turns a selector or media condition into a reusable prefix
cards.use: want a prefix for a theme or condition Tailwind has no name for

cards.subject: The Prettier plugin for Tailwind
says: sorts class names into a consistent order
changes only the order of classes, not the styling
cards.use: want every developer's class strings in the same order

cards.subject: Tailwind CSS IntelliSense
says: autocompletes class names in the editor
shows the CSS a class produces on hover
cards.use: want the editor to suggest valid class names as you type

cards.subject: Extracting a component
says: wraps a repeated markup-and-class pattern in a reusable component
keeps one source of truth for the markup and not just the classes
cards.use: see the same card markup and classes on many pages
not: copies the class string into a CSS file

cards.subject: @apply
says: inlines existing utilities into a custom CSS rule
builds a named class out of utilities
cards.use: need a named class for markup you do not control
not: adds a utility to the generated stylesheet without any CSS rule

cards.subject: @layer components
says: places custom classes where utilities can still override them
keeps hand-written classes lower in the cascade than utilities
cards.use: write a .btn class that a utility can still adjust

cards.subject: A list rendered in a loop
says: repeats a class string many times on the page while writing it once in source
makes duplicated output harmless to maintain
cards.use: worry about the same classes appearing on fifty list rows

cards.subject: Variant props
says: choose among predefined class sets such as primary or ghost
keep one component covering several looks
cards.use: need one Button component to render primary and secondary looks

cards.subject: Overusing @apply
says: recreates the naming and sync problems utilities were meant to avoid
hides which utilities an element really uses
not: is the recommended default for every element

cards.subject: A named class such as .btn
says: suits a tiny pattern shared by many unrelated places
lives in the global stylesheet rather than in a component
cards.use: need one small look shared by plain HTML as well as components

cards.subject: Copy-pasting class strings
says: turns a design change into a search across many files
is the main reason to extract components

cards.subject: Content scanning
says: searches source files for class-name tokens
generates CSS only for the class names it finds
cards.use: wonder how Tailwind decides which CSS to emit

cards.subject: A complete class name
says: must appear as a whole string in the source to be detected
is found by the scanner even inside a plain string or object value
cards.use: write a class name inside a conditional expression
not: can be assembled from pieces at runtime and still be detected

cards.subject: Dynamic class construction such as text-${color}-500
says: builds a name the scanner never sees as a whole
leaves the class out of the stylesheet
not: is detected because the pieces appear in the file
like: A lookup object of full class names

cards.subject: A lookup object of full class names
says: lists each complete class once so the scanner can see it
maps a status or variant to its classes
like: Dynamic class construction such as text-${color}-500

cards.subject: Safelisting
says: forces named classes to be generated even when no file contains them
covers classes that arrive from a database or CMS
cards.use: receive class names as strings from a CMS at runtime
not: is the normal way to handle every conditional class

cards.subject: Adding a source path
says: tells the scanner to look in files outside its default locations
is needed when components live in a separate package
cards.use: find that components from a shared package come out unstyled

cards.subject: The PostCSS plugin
says: runs Tailwind as a step in the CSS build
is registered in postcss.config.mjs
cards.use: need Tailwind to run inside a bundler that uses PostCSS

cards.subject: On-demand generation
says: emits a rule when a class is first found rather than shipping a prebuilt list
makes arbitrary values possible
cards.use: wonder how bg-[#070b1a] can work without being in a list

cards.subject: The dark: variant
says: applies a utility when dark mode is active
is stacked on a base class such as bg-white dark:bg-slate-900
cards.use: want a white card to turn dark in dark mode

cards.subject: prefers-color-scheme
says: is the CSS media feature that reports the user's operating-system theme
lets a page follow the OS light or dark setting
cards.use: want the page to follow the device theme
not: is a JavaScript API you must call to read the theme

cards.subject: Media-based dark mode
says: follows the operating system's colour-scheme preference
needs no toggle or JavaScript
cards.use: want dark mode with no code and no toggle button
not: lets the user override the OS from a button without any other code

cards.subject: Selector-based dark mode
says: activates dark styles from a class or attribute on an ancestor
needs JavaScript to set and remember the user's choice
cards.use: want a visible light-dark toggle that overrides the OS

cards.subject: Token-driven dark mode
says: swaps CSS variable values so components carry no dark: classes
keeps theme logic in one stylesheet rather than in every component
cards.use: want dark mode without touching every component's class list

cards.subject: A dark-only design
says: ships a single dark palette with no light variant
needs no toggle and no dark: classes
cards.use: build a product that only has one dark look

cards.subject: A stored theme preference applied after render
says: causes a flash of the wrong theme
is avoided by setting the theme attribute before first paint

cards.subject: Designing dark colours
says: picks each shade for contrast rather than inverting the light palette
may switch the text on an accent fill to a dark colour
cards.use: find that an inverted palette makes accent buttons hard to read

cards.subject: sr-only
says: hides content visually while keeping it available to screen readers
gives an icon-only button its text label
cards.use: need an accessible name for an icon-only button
not: removes the element from the accessibility tree like display none

cards.subject: focus:not-sr-only
says: reveals visually hidden content when the element receives focus
is the usual way to build a skip link
cards.use: want a skip-to-content link that appears only for keyboard users

cards.subject: focus-visible:ring-2
says: gives keyboard users a visible focus indicator
adds a ring for focus from the keyboard

cards.subject: outline-none
says: removes the default focus outline
is an accessibility problem unless another focus indicator replaces it
not: is the recommended default for every button

cards.subject: The motion-reduce: variant
says: applies a utility when the user prefers reduced motion
turns off animation for people sensitive to movement
cards.use: want a spinner or parallax effect to stop for users who request less motion

cards.subject: The hidden utility
says: removes an element from layout and the accessibility tree
hides content from sighted users and screen readers alike
cards.use: want content absent for everyone

cards.subject: Utility classes and semantics
says: change appearance but never add semantics or keyboard behaviour
leave a styled div without button behaviour
not: turn a div into a button for assistive technology

cards.subject: Colour as the only state signal
says: fails users who cannot tell the colours apart
is fixed by adding an icon, text or underline

cards.subject: Small generated CSS
says: stays small because only used utilities are emitted
grows with distinct classes, not with how often each is used
cards.use: wonder why the stylesheet is small despite a huge framework

cards.subject: Production minification
says: compresses the generated stylesheet in a production build
removes whitespace and comments from the output
cards.use: ship the stylesheet in a production build

cards.subject: No runtime cost
says: means nothing is computed in the browser to produce styles
contrasts with runtime CSS-in-JS
cards.use: compare utility CSS with a library that builds styles in JavaScript

cards.subject: Animating transform and opacity
says: is cheaper for the browser than animating width or height
avoids re-flowing the layout on every frame
cards.use: want a smooth hover animation on a card

cards.subject: An over-wide safelist
says: inflates the stylesheet with classes never used
is a cost paid by every visitor

cards.subject: Many unique arbitrary values
says: each generate their own rule, so the stylesheet grows
are a sign to add tokens to the theme

cards.subject: className
says: is the React prop that receives a Tailwind class string
replaces the HTML class attribute name in JSX
cards.use: write a Tailwind class string on a JSX element
not: is spelled class in JSX

cards.subject: A global stylesheet imported in the root layout
says: loads the Tailwind CSS for every page of a Next.js app
makes the utilities available to all routes without per-page imports
cards.use: need Tailwind styles on every route of a Next.js app

cards.subject: A template literal with a ternary
says: chooses between full class names at render time
works as long as every complete class name appears in the source
cards.use: need a class to depend on a boolean prop
not: lets you build class names from fragments

cards.subject: clsx
says: joins class names conditionally and drops falsy values
does not know that two Tailwind classes conflict
cards.use: need to combine several conditional class names cleanly
not: resolves p-4 versus p-8 conflicts for you

cards.subject: tailwind-merge
says: removes earlier conflicting utilities when a later one targets the same property
lets a component accept a className override safely
cards.use: need a caller's px-8 to beat a component's default px-4

cards.subject: class-variance-authority
says: declares component variants as a map from props to class strings
gives a Button typed primary and secondary options
cards.use: want a typed variant API for a Button

cards.subject: Server Components with Tailwind
says: need no special handling because Tailwind emits static CSS
can use className exactly like client components
cards.use: wonder whether Tailwind works in Server Components

cards.subject: A className prop on a component
says: lets callers adjust a component's layout without forking it
is usually merged with the component's own classes
cards.use: want a Card that callers can position from outside

cards.subject: A CSS variable passed through the style prop
says: carries a runtime number into a bracket class such as w-[var(--w)]
keeps the class name static while the value changes
cards.use: need a progress bar width from data

cards.subject: Tailwind in our apps
says: is listed as tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/postcss in package.json
is on major version 4 with the minor not pinned
cards.use: need to check which Tailwind major gglearn and ggsocial use

cards.subject: postcss.config.mjs
says: registers the @tailwindcss/postcss plugin
is where each app wires Tailwind into the build
cards.use: look for where Tailwind is registered in gglearn

cards.subject: The missing tailwind.config file
says: means configuration lives in CSS
shows the apps use CSS-first configuration
cards.use: wonder why gglearn has no tailwind.config file

cards.subject: @import "tailwindcss"
says: starts app/globals.css
pulls Tailwind's layers into the stylesheet
cards.use: need the first line of the globals.css

cards.subject: The ggsocial :root tokens
says: define --bg, --surface, --border, --text, --muted and --accent as variables
hold the light-theme values
cards.use: need to know where ggsocial's colours are defined

cards.subject: The ggsocial @theme inline block
says: maps variables such as --surface to --color-surface
makes utilities such as bg-surface-2 and text-muted exist
cards.use: wonder why bg-surface-2 works in ggsocial

cards.subject: The gglearn colour tokens
says: set --background and --foreground in :root
are mapped to color-background and color-foreground by @theme inline
cards.use: need to know how gglearn exposes its colours to utilities

cards.subject: The gglearn dark mode
says: is dark-only, with no light theme to switch to
uses no dark: variant classes in its components
cards.use: wonder whether gglearn has a theme toggle

cards.subject: The ggsocial dark mode
says: follows the system theme through a prefers-color-scheme media query
lets data-theme="light" force light even when the OS is dark
cards.use: need to know how ggsocial chooses light or dark

cards.subject: The gglearn named classes
says: are .card, .btn and .gradient-text in globals.css
keep repeated looks while layout stays as utilities
cards.use: look for where gglearn keeps its card and button styles

cards.subject: The ggsocial components/ui.tsx
says: holds its own Card, Button and Field built from utilities
is preferred over copying long class strings
cards.use: look for ggsocial's shared UI primitives

cards.subject: Unlayered rules in globals.css
says: beat every Tailwind utility regardless of specificity
make a rule like button { color: inherit } override text-accent-fg
cards.use: see a utility ignored because of a plain global rule
not: are overridden by every utility because their specificity is lower

cards.subject: The shared kit's base.css
says: would fight Tailwind's preflight reset
is never imported; only styles.css is
cards.use: wire the shared gg-ui kit into ggsocial

cards.subject: The Linux Tailwind native binary
says: is skipped by npm ci when the lockfile was generated on macOS
is fixed on the server with an explicit npm install --no-save pinned to the installed oxide version
cards.use: see a cannot-find-module error for @tailwindcss/oxide-linux-x64-gnu during a server build

qa.q: What does this class string do to the element's children?
qa.right: Lays them in a row, vertically centred, with equal space between them
wrong: Stacks them in a column with no spacing
Turns each child into its own grid
Hides every child except the first
qa.why: flex makes a row, items-center centres on the cross axis and gap-4 spaces the children.

qa.q: With the default spacing scale, how much padding does p-4 add?
qa.right: 1rem on all four sides
qa.why: One spacing step is 0.25rem, so step 4 is 1rem.

qa.q: What does Tailwind put in the stylesheet it generates?
qa.right: Only the CSS for the class names it finds in your source files
wrong: Every utility it can possibly produce
Only the classes used on the first page
A copy of every class from node_modules
qa.why: Content scanning keeps the output small.

qa.q: In this markup, when does the background change?
qa.right: While the pointer is over the button
wrong: Only after the button is clicked
qa.why: The hover: prefix applies the utility under the hover condition.

qa.q: What does rounded-full do on a square image with equal width and height?
qa.right: Makes it a circle
wrong: Crops it to a half-height rectangle
qa.why: A full radius on a square produces a circle.

qa.q: Which prop do you use to give a JSX element Tailwind classes?
qa.right: className
qa.why: JSX uses className for the HTML class attribute.

qa.q: On a 900px wide screen, how wide is this element, and how wide on a 500px screen?
qa.right: Half its parent on the 900px screen, full width on the 500px screen
wrong: Full width at 900px and half at 500px
qa.why: The unprefixed class is the mobile base; md: applies from 768px upward.

qa.q: Which class string is small text on phones and larger text from md upward?
qa.right: text-sm md:text-lg
qa.why: Tailwind is mobile-first, so the base class is the smallest layout and the prefix adds the change.

qa.q: Why is the span in this button there?
qa.right: It gives the icon-only button an accessible name that only screen readers see
wrong: It makes the button load faster
It adds a tooltip for mouse users
It removes the button from the tab order
qa.why: sr-only hides content visually while keeping it in the accessibility tree.

qa.q: What does bg-black/50 mean?
qa.right: A black background at fifty percent opacity
wrong: A black background at fifty pixels
Black on the first of fifty states
A background that is fifty percent black and fifty percent white
qa.why: The slash suffix is the opacity modifier.

qa.q: What must be on the parent for this link to underline when the card is hovered?
qa.right: The group class
qa.why: group-hover: styles a child from a marked ancestor.

qa.q: What does mx-auto need in order to centre a block?
qa.right: A set width or max width smaller than the parent
wrong: A text-center on the block itself
qa.why: Automatic side margins only share leftover space when the block does not fill the parent.

qa.q: What is the difference between h-screen and min-h-screen?
qa.right: min-h-screen lets the element grow taller than the viewport when content needs it
wrong: h-screen grows with content, min-h-screen does not
qa.why: h-screen fixes the height; min-h-screen sets only a floor.

qa.q: What does the first line of app/globals.css do in our apps?
qa.right: Loads Tailwind with an @import of tailwindcss
qa.why: Configuration is CSS-first and starts with the import.

qa.q: Why does this component sometimes lose its colour?
qa.right: The scanner cannot see the full class name, so the CSS may never be generated
wrong: Template literals are not allowed in JSX
qa.why: Class names must appear as whole strings.

qa.q: In this markup, what makes the label bold?
qa.right: The checkbox being checked, because the peer comes before the label
wrong: The label being the first child
Any checkbox anywhere on the page
qa.why: peer-checked: reads the state of a preceding sibling.

qa.q: What does this CSS do?
qa.right: Copies the declarations of those utilities into the .btn rule
wrong: Defines the utilities for the first time
Loads the utilities from a CDN
qa.why: @apply inlines existing utilities into a custom rule.

qa.q: What does this grid do from md upward?
qa.right: Uses three columns with spacing, and one column below md
wrong: Uses one column from md upward
Uses three columns on phones and one on desktop
qa.why: The unprefixed grid-cols-1 is the base and md: overrides it.

qa.q: What does the underscore in this class stand for?
qa.right: A space between the two track sizes
qa.why: Underscores in arbitrary values become spaces.

qa.q: What does this combination do?
qa.right: Passes a runtime value into a class that stays static for the scanner
wrong: Builds a new class name at runtime
Forces the class into the safelist
qa.why: The style prop carries the variable; the class refers to it.

qa.q: What is wrong with this button for keyboard users?
qa.right: It shows no focus indicator when tabbed to
wrong: It is invisible to screen readers
qa.why: outline-none removes the default outline and nothing replaces it.
qa.code: <button class="rounded bg-blue-600 px-4 py-2 text-white outline-none">Save</button>

qa.q: Which colour wins here?
qa.right: It depends on the order of rules in the generated stylesheet, not the class order
qa.why: Class attribute order does not decide conflicts.

qa.q: What does the dark: part of this class do?
qa.right: Applies bg-slate-900 when dark mode is active
qa.why: The dark: variant is conditional on dark mode.

qa.q: Which dark mode strategy follows the OS with no JavaScript and no toggle?
qa.right: Media-based dark mode using prefers-color-scheme
wrong: A class on the html element
A data attribute set by a script
qa.why: The media feature reports the OS preference directly.

qa.q: Why add motion-reduce:animate-none here?
qa.right: To stop the animation for users who ask for reduced motion
qa.why: motion-reduce: reacts to the user's reduced motion preference.

qa.q: What does this do?
qa.right: Hides the nav below md and shows it as flex from md upward
wrong: Shows it below md and hides it above
qa.why: hidden is the base, md:flex replaces it.

qa.q: What does truncate do to a single line of overflowing text?
qa.right: Clips it and ends it with an ellipsis
wrong: Wraps it onto a new line
Removes the overflowing words from the DOM
qa.why: It combines overflow clipping, an ellipsis and no wrapping.

qa.q: Why use the typography plugin on a blog?
qa.right: To style markdown-rendered HTML you cannot put classes on
qa.why: A prose wrapper styles headings, lists and quotes in raw HTML.

qa.q: What is the result when isActive is true?
qa.right: px-4 bg-blue-500
qa.why: clsx adds truthy conditional entries and drops falsy ones.

qa.q: What happens to the link on hover?
qa.right: The text turns white with a smooth transition
qa.why: transition animates the colour change added by hover:.

qa.q: Why does gap-4 beat space-x-4 for a list that wraps?
qa.right: gap spaces rows and columns properly when items wrap, margin-based spacing does not
wrong: gap works only on one line
qa.why: Selector-based margins do not handle a second line of wrapped items well.

qa.q: What does flex-col change about items-center?
qa.right: It centres items horizontally, because the cross axis is now horizontal
wrong: It centres items vertically as before
qa.why: items-* aligns on the cross axis, which flips with the direction.

qa.q: A status badge colour arrives from the API as red or green. What is the safe way to style it?
qa.right: Map each status to a full class name in a lookup object
wrong: Build bg-${colour}-100 with a template literal
Add every colour to a runtime style tag
qa.why: Complete class names must be visible to the scanner.

qa.q: A team added a global rule and now text-accent-fg is ignored on buttons. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: The global rule sits outside any layer and beats every utility
wrong: The class is misspelled in the config
qa.why: Unlayered rules beat layered utilities regardless of specificity; keep base rules in @layer base.

qa.q: npm ci succeeds but the Linux server build fails with cannot find module @tailwindcss/oxide-linux-x64-gnu. What is the fix?
qa.right: Run an explicit npm install --no-save pinned to the installed oxide version on the server
wrong: Delete Tailwind and use inline styles
qa.why: The lockfile generated on macOS lacks the Linux binary, so the fix stays out of the lockfile.

qa.q: Components from a shared workspace package render unstyled in the app. What should you check first?
qa.right: That the scanner is told to include the package's source path
wrong: That the package uses class instead of className
qa.why: The scanner only reads files it knows about.

qa.q: What does inline do in this block?
qa.right: References the variable itself instead of copying its value, so runtime changes flow through
wrong: Makes the colour apply only to inline elements
Compiles the colour to hex at build time
qa.why: With inline, utilities keep pointing at var(--surface).

qa.q: Users see a white flash before a dark page appears. What is the cause?
qa.right: The stored theme preference is applied after the first paint
wrong: Dark mode needs a bigger stylesheet
The dark: variant is disabled in production
The viewport meta tag is missing
qa.why: Set the theme attribute before the page paints.

qa.q: What does this link do, and when is it visible?
qa.right: It is hidden until it receives keyboard focus, then it appears so users can skip to content
wrong: It is removed from the page
It is visible only to screen readers always
qa.why: sr-only plus focus:not-sr-only builds a skip link.

qa.q: A Button has px-4 and a caller passes className="px-8". How do you make the caller win reliably?
qa.right: Merge the classes with tailwind-merge
wrong: Put px-8 first in the string
qa.why: Class order does not decide; tailwind-merge drops the earlier conflicting utility.

qa.q: Why use aria-expanded:rotate-180 on a chevron?
qa.right: The visual state follows the accessibility state without extra JavaScript toggling a class
wrong: It works without aria-expanded being set
It rotates every chevron on the page
qa.why: Tying style to the ARIA attribute keeps both in sync.

qa.q: When does this underline show?
qa.right: On hover, and only from md upward
qa.why: Stacked variants all must be true.

qa.q: What does this selector variant style?
qa.right: The direct li children of the list
qa.why: The arbitrary variant writes the selector in brackets.

qa.q: The same 12-class string is pasted into forty files. What is the best first step?
qa.right: Extract a component that owns the markup and classes
wrong: Add the classes to a safelist
qa.why: A component keeps one source of truth for markup and classes.

qa.q: A card needs to reflow when its sidebar slot is narrow even on a wide screen. Which feature fits?
qa.right: Container query variants
qa.why: Viewport breakpoints cannot see the slot size.

qa.q: Your team wants every component styled through an @apply class. What is the main risk?
qa.right: It recreates naming and sync problems and hides which utilities an element uses
qa.why: Utility-first markup avoids both problems.

qa.q: Why do hundreds of bracket values like w-[37px] signal a problem?
qa.right: Each distinct value generates its own rule, and the repeated values belong in the theme
wrong: They are rejected by the scanner
qa.why: Promote repeated values to tokens.

qa.q: Why pick transition-transform with a scale hover over animating width?
qa.right: Transform animation avoids re-flowing layout on every frame
wrong: width cannot be animated in CSS
qa.why: Transform and opacity are cheaper to animate.

qa.q: A brand blue is typed as bg-[#1d4ed8] in sixty places and the brand is changing. What should have been done?
qa.right: Add a named colour token to the theme and use its utility
wrong: Turn the colour into a template literal
qa.why: A token gives the value one place to change.

qa.q: A .card class in plain global CSS keeps beating p-6 on the same element. Why, and what is the fix?
qa.right: Unlayered rules beat utilities, so move it into @layer components
wrong: p-6 is not a real utility
Specificity of classes is equal, so the first wins
The card class needs !important in markup
qa.why: Layered utilities lose to unlayered rules.

qa.q: What does this class string need for the headline to show a colour gradient?
qa.right: A gradient background to be present, since the text is transparent
wrong: Nothing else, transparent shows a gradient automatically
qa.why: bg-clip-text clips the background to the letters and text-transparent reveals it.

qa.q: What does cn do in this component?
qa.right: Joins conditional classes and resolves Tailwind conflicts so the caller's classes win
wrong: Adds the classes to the safelist
qa.why: cn is typically twMerge(clsx(...)).

qa.q: Deploy fixed the build error but the same failure still shows. What does ggsocial's DEPLOY.md warn about?
qa.right: Turbopack can cache a failed build
qa.why: The cache must be cleared before the fixed build is trusted.
